slot.brief: Position vector given as function of time; differentiate to get velocity/acceleration at an instant

stem: The position vector of a particle is $r(t)=(t^2+3t)i+(2t^2-t)j$ m, where $t$ is in seconds. What is its velocity at $t=2$ s?

verdicts.working: Differentiate each component: v(t)=(2t+3)i+(4t-1)j. At t=2, v=7i+7j m·s⁻¹.

working:
$v_x=\dfrac{d}{dt}(t^2+3t)=2t+3$, $v_y=\dfrac{d}{dt}(2t^2-t)=4t-1$; at $t=2$ s, $\vec v=(7i+7j)\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$.

Independent check: Differentiate each component: v(t)=(2t+3)i+(4t-1)j. At t=2, v=7i+7j m·s⁻¹.
solution:
Velocity is the time derivative of position:
$$\vec v(t)=(2t+3)\mathbf i+(4t-1)\mathbf j.$$
At $t=2\,\mathrm{s}$, $\vec v=(7\mathbf i+7\mathbf j)\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$.
